title: Perplexity Open Sources 9B and 0.6B Embedding Models for OCR-Free Search
summary:
Perplexity has launched a set of late-interaction embedding models that allow for the retrieval of text and images within a single shared vector space. The new pplx-embed-v2-late weights are hosted on Hugging Face and enable users to search across PDF pages, screenshots, and slide decks as images, eliminating the need for optical character recognition. The framework is natively supported in Sentence Transformers and facilitates cross-model querying, where data is indexed by a larger model and queried by a smaller one to reduce latency.

The models, available in 9B and 0.6B parameter versions, scored 92.4% on MADQA and 64% on BrowseComp+. Across 72 text retrieval tasks, the 9B model achieved 81.3 nDCG@10, while the 0.6B version reached 78.0. Perplexity reports that pairing 0.6B queries with 9B indexing improves text retrieval to 79.6 nDCG@10, and the 0.6B model's performance on ViDoRe v3 page images is within 1.2 points of the Nemotron ColEmbed V2 8B.

You can use these to index multimodal data with 9B, and query on device with 0.6B. This also enables you to search over PDF pages with no OCR. And scores 92.4% on MADQA, 64% on BrowseComp+. Weights available on @huggingface now.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Perplexity reports that 0.6B queries + 9B documents improves over 0.6B on both sides
selectedTweets.text:
Perplexity reports that 0.6B queries + 9B documents improves over 0.6B on both sides:

- Text, six-domain average: 78.0 → 79.6 nDCG@10
- ViDoRe v3 images: 62.3 → 63.5 nDCG@10

So this means you can get closer to the 9B perf. with a 0.6B query latency. https://t.co/JV4BcPokmW

selectedTweets.bestBit: The 0.6B is within 1.2 points of Nemotron ColEmbed V2 8B
selectedTweets.text:
On public ViDoRe v3 page images, Perplexity reports:

- 0.6B: 62.3 nDCG@10
- 9B: 65.2 nDCG@10

The 0.6B is within 1.2 points of Nemotron ColEmbed V2 8B. The size-vs-quality plot is particularly nice here. https://t.co/BC2jbOy97F
